theorem actual_all_input_coordinate_halfspace_distance
    (i : I) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
    Metric.infDist x {y : EuclideanSpace ℝ I | y i ≤ 0}=max (x i) 0

theorem actual_every_real_normed_unit_ball_has_the_printed_all_input_distance
    {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (x : V) :
    Metric.infDist x (Metric.closedBall (0:V) 1)=max (‖x‖-1) 0

theorem actual_all_real_radii_infinity_balls_are_coordinate_boxes
    [Nonempty I] (x x0 : I → ℝ) (epsilon : ℝ) :
    ‖x-x0‖ ≤ epsilon ↔ ∀ i,|x i-x0 i| ≤ epsilon

theorem actual_rectangular_grid_edges_are_exactly_horizontal_or_vertical_unit_steps
    (r c : ℕ) (u v : Fin (r+1) × Fin (c+1)) :
    (rectangularGrid r c).Adj u v ↔
    ((u.1.val+1=v.1.val ∨ v.1.val+1=u.1.val) ∧ u.2=v.2) ∨
    ((u.2.val+1=v.2.val ∨ v.2.val+1=u.2.val) ∧ u.1=v.1)

theorem actual_rectangular_grid_is_connected (r c : ℕ) :
    (rectangularGrid r c).Connected

theorem actual_rectangular_grid_shortest_path_length_is_a_real_metric
    (r c : ℕ) (u v w : Fin (r+1) × Fin (c+1)) :
    (0 ≤ ((rectangularGrid r c).dist u v : ℝ)) ∧
    (((rectangularGrid r c).dist u v : ℝ)=0 ↔ u=v) ∧
    ((rectangularGrid r c).dist u v : ℝ)=((rectangularGrid r c).dist v u : ℝ) ∧
    ((rectangularGrid r c).dist u w : ℝ) ≤
      ((rectangularGrid r c).dist u v : ℝ)+((rectangularGrid r c).dist v w : ℝ) ∧
    ∃ p : (rectangularGrid r c).Walk u v,
      p.length=(rectangularGrid r c).dist u v ∧
      ∀ q : (rectangularGrid r c).Walk u v,p.length ≤ q.length

theorem actual_Lipschitz_values_have_the_printed_lower_margin
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (g : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0)
    (hg : LipschitzWith L g) (y z : X) : g z-(L:ℝ)*dist y z ≤ g y

theorem actual_union_of_all_positive_value_Lipschitz_balls_is_certified
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (g : X → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0)
    (hg : LipschitzWith L g) (hL : 0 < (L:ℝ)) :
    ∀ y∈{y | ∃ z,0 < g z ∧ y∈Metric.closedBall z (g z/L)},0 ≤ g y

theorem actual_zero_Lipschitz_constant_certifies_the_entire_domain_without_division
    {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (g : X → ℝ) (hg : LipschitzWith 0 g)
    (z : X) (hz : 0 < g z) : ∀ y, g y=g z ∧ 0 < g y

theorem actual_every_connected_grid_or_other_graph_has_an_attained_shortest_path_metric
    {X : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph X) (hG : G.Connected) (u v w : X) :
    ((G.dist u v : ℝ)=0 ↔ u=v) ∧
    (G.dist u v : ℝ)=(G.dist v u : ℝ) ∧
    (G.dist u w : ℝ) ≤ (G.dist u v : ℝ)+(G.dist v w : ℝ) ∧
    ∃ p : G.Walk u v,p.length=G.dist u v ∧ ∀ q : G.Walk u v,p.length ≤ q.length

entire_current_literal.source_text: Examples. $\mathrm{dist}(x,\{x_1\le0\})=\max\{x_1,0\}$; for the unit disc, $\max\{\|x\|_2-1,0\}$. The $\ell_\infty$ ball $\{\|x-x_0\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\}$ is the box $|x_i-x_{0,i}|\le\varepsilon$, handled coordinate by coordinate by interval methods. Shortest-path length on a grid is a metric too. Certified balls: if $g$ is $L$-Lipschitz with $L\gt0$ and $g(z)=c\gt0$, then $g\ge0$ on $B_{c/L}(z)$, since $g(y)\ge c-L\,d(y,z)$; a union of such balls is certified. If $L=0$, the Lipschitz inequality makes $g$ constant on its domain, so the positive value at $z$ certifies the whole domain; no division by zero is needed.

primer-linalg.html::node-202.context_domain_read: The vector examples use their ordinary nonempty finite coordinate domain (the first clause names x1), the disc is planar Euclidean, grid means an ordinary connected nearest-neighbour grid, and certificates use the declared metric domain D. These domains agree with the actual all-input proofs and need no new wording proposal.

all_input_coordinate_halfspace_distance.domain: Every finite Euclidean coordinate type with an actual coordinate i, every input x; an explicit single-coordinate projection supplies the attained upper bound and every halfspace point supplies the norm lower bound.

all_input_unit_disc_distance.domain: The actual closed unit-ball formula is derived in every real normed vector space at every input, including its inside and outside radial branches; the literal planar Euclidean unit disc is its specialization.

all_real_radii_infinity_coordinate_boxes.domain: Every nonempty finite real coordinate type, every x,x0 and real epsilon. Negative-radius sets are both empty, the zero-radius set is the center, and each positive-radius condition is exactly the independent coordinate interval.

actual_rectangular_grid_metric_and_attai.domain: Every complete rectangular nearest-neighbour grid Fin(r+1) times Fin(c+1), including one-vertex dimensions: exact unit-step adjacency, derived connectivity, real shortest-path metric axioms and a genuinely attained minimum walk length.

arbitrary_connected_graph_metric_and_att.domain: Every structurally connected graph, finite or infinite. This does not assign a finite metric to an arbitrary disconnected obstacle mask; library unreachable-pair junk value0 is explicitly excluded by connectivity.

actual_Lipschitz_margin_positive_ball_an.domain: Global LipschitzWith L on the declared (pseudo)metric domain, with L>0. The lower margin is derived and each actual positive-center closed ball and the entire union have g>=0; balls are relative to that domain.

zero_Lipschitz_entire_domain.domain: LipschitzWith0 on the declared domain yields equality of every two values; one positive center certifies every domain point without division.
